html:
Adi Shankara was a Hindu monk and philosopher of the 8th century, born in Kerala, who became the great teacher of Advaita Vedanta. Its core claim is that only Brahman, the one reality, truly exists, and that the self is not different from it.

He set out this view in commentaries on the Upanishads, the Brahma Sutras and the Bhagavad Gita. These three texts were the base of Vedanta, and his readings of them set the terms for later debate.

Tradition says he walked the length of India, argued with Buddhist and Hindu rivals, and founded four monasteries at the corners of the land, among them Sringeri in the south. It also says he died at 32. Very little about his life is certain, and some scholars think his fame grew mostly in later centuries.

Later thinkers defined themselves against him. Ramanuja in the 11th century argued for a God with real qualities and devotion to him, a line that fed the bhakti movement. Today Shankara is often called the most important philosopher of Hinduism.
